arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: BP counsel argued the statute mandates review. He cited the federal officer exception. He claimed the text is clear. He rejected the need for a valid claim. He emphasized the plain language of the law. He argued against judicial discretion in this context. He sought a bright-line rule for appeals. He warned against expanding state court power.

Baltimore counsel argued the statute requires validity. He cited the purpose of the removal law. He claimed a frivolous claim cannot trigger review. He emphasized the need for a proper basis. He warned against strategic abuse of the process. He argued for a reasonable interpretation. He sought to preserve state court authority. He focused on the practical consequences.

Justices questioned the practical implications of the interpretations. They probed the definition of a valid claim. They examined the consequences of allowing frivolous appeals. They considered the impact on state courts. They asked about the role of judicial discretion. They explored the balance between federal and state power. They sought clarity on the statutory text.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: BP seeks to remove a state case to federal court. It cites the federal officer statute. The district court rejects the claim and remands the case. BP wants to appeal that remand order. Baltimore argues the appeal is barred. The dispute centers on Section 1447(d). This statute limits appeals of remand orders. It creates an exception for federal officer claims.

It preserves the integrity of the removal process.
